what.text: This page follows asylum seekers from Russia in South Korea: people who have asked for international protection and are waiting for a decision.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 7835 Russian asylum seekers in South Korea, 8.9% of all asylum seekers from Russia.

why.text: UCDP records an interstate armed conflict between Russia and Ukraine from 2022 to 2025, at war level in each of those years.
It also records armed conflict over the government of Russia in 2023 and 2024, with LSR, RDK and Wagner as opponents.

when.text: UNHCR's series for this group starts in 2007 at 5 asylum seekers, and the figure was at its highest, 8669, at the end of 2024.
The main years of displacement in the data are 2023 to 2025.

how.text: The sources don't say which routes people took or where they live in South Korea.
Asylum seekers are counted separately from refugees, as year-end totals for South Korea only.
